mainEntity.name: How much does a Volvo S60 or V60 diesel engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volvo S60 or V60 diesel engine replacement typically costs £3,200-£5,500 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £4,000-£7,000 depending on the engine code and labour rates. The D4204T14 (D4) and D5244T15 (D5) are the most common diesel engines in UK S60s and V60s. Used engines: £900-£3,200. Reconditioned: £2,000-£5,500. Rebuilt with warranty: £3,000-£7,500. Fitting labour: 8-14 hours at £65-£100/hr.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EGR valve failure in a Volvo S60 or V60 diesel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include loss of power, rough idling, increased fuel consumption and a check engine light. The EGR valve becomes clogged with soot over time. On modern 2.0-litre D3, D4 and D5 units, clogging is more common than on older 2.4-litre engines. Loss of power and poor throttle response. Rough idling or engine hesitation. Check engine light with EGR-related fault codes. Increased fuel consumption.

mainEntity.name: When should the timing belt be replaced on a Volvo S60 or V60 diesel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Volvo recommends replacing the timing belt every 140,000 km (approx 87,000 miles) or 10 years, whichever comes first. Many specialists recommend 60,000-80,000 miles or 8 years. Tensioners are prone to failure and may not last the scheduled interval. 60,000-80,000 miles: recommended for peace of mind. 87,000 miles or 10 years: Volvo's official interval. If auxiliary belt fails, it can take the timing belt with it.

mainEntity.name: Is the Volvo D5 diesel engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the D5 is considered one of Volvo's most robust diesel engines. The 2.4-litre five-cylinder D5 (D5244T10, D5244T11, D5244T15) is particularly well-regarded for its durability and refinement. However, injector failure and EGR/DPF issues are common at higher mileages. 5-cylinder D5: very reliable, known for longevity. Injector failure: common from 80,000 miles. Regular maintenance is essential - especially timing belt and oil changes.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Volvo D3, D4 and D5 diesel engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The D3, D4 and D5 are power output variants of Volvo's diesel engines. The D3 is the entry-level diesel (136-150 hp), the D4 is the mid-range (163-190 hp) and the D5 is the top-tier diesel (205-235 hp). Early models used five-cylinder engines (D5204T, D5244T); later models use four-cylinder Drive-E (VEA) engines (D4204T). D3: 136-150 hp, 2.0-litre (5-cyl or 4-cyl). D4: 163-190 hp, 2.0-litre (5-cyl or 4-cyl). D5: 205-235 hp, 2.4-litre (5-cyl) or 2.0-litre (4-cyl).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volvo S60 or V60 diesel?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and what has failed. For a 2014-2019 S60 or V60 D4 worth £4,000-£12,000, a £3,200-£5,500 rebuilt engine is usually worthwhile if the car is otherwise sound. For a 2010-2013 example worth under £4,000, a used engine or repair may be more cost-effective. Cars worth £6,000+: rebuilt engine with warranty is recommended. Cars worth £3,000-£6,000: evaluate both options. Cars worth under £3,000: consider used engine or scrap. Timing belt failure: often cheaper to replace the engine than repair the damage.

historyTimeline.h2: Volvo S60 / V60 D3 D4 D5 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The D3, D4 and D5 diesel badges have defined the diesel line-up for the Volvo S60 and V60 since the second-generation (P3) models launched in 2010. Originally powered by five-cylinder 2.0-litre and 2.4-litre turbo diesels, the range transitioned to the more efficient four-cylinder Drive-E (VEA) engines from 2014 onwards. The D5 badge has always represented the most powerful diesel option, with the D3 and D4 offering varying power outputs through the years.

milestones.description: D5204T2, 2.0-litre five-cylinder turbo diesel, 163 hp - original D3 engine (later rebadged D4)
D5244T10, 2.4-litre five-cylinder turbo diesel, 205 hp - original D5 engine
D5244T11, 2.4-litre five-cylinder twin-turbo diesel, 215 hp - revised D5 with increased power
D5204T7, 2.0-litre five-cylinder turbo diesel, 136 hp - new entry-level D3
D5244T15, 2.4-litre five-cylinder twin-turbo diesel, 215 hp - updated D5 with improved emissions
D4204T14, 2.0-litre four-cylinder Drive-E diesel, 190 hp - new D4 replacing the five-cylinder D3/D4
D4204T9, 2.0-litre four-cylinder Drive-E diesel, 150 hp - new D3 variant
D4204T11, 2.0-litre four-cylinder Drive-E diesel, 225 hp - high-output D5 variant
D4204T23, 2.0-litre four-cylinder Drive-E diesel, 235 hp - D5 AWD variant

commonProblems.h2: Volvo S60 / V60 D3 D4 D5 Diesel Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volvo S60 and V60 D3, D4 and D5 diesel engines are generally well-regarded for their durability and refinement. However, they have specific, well-documented failure points - particularly around the EGR system, injectors and timing belts. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR Valve & DPF Clogging - The Most Common Volvo S60 / V60 Diesel Problem
problems.affectedModels: Volvo S60 and V60 (all D3, D4 and D5 diesel variants)
problems.rootCause: The EGR (Exhaust Gas Recirculation) system recycles exhaust gases but leaves thick soot deposits. While older 2.4-litre engines were resilient, modern 2.0-litre D3, D4 and D5 units are prone to clogging. The DPF (Diesel Particulate Filter) also becomes blocked, particularly with urban driving. The EGR valve is a dealer-only part costing approximately £550 plus VAT.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve and intake

repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix if valve is faulty

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Forced DPF regeneration or chemical clean

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2016 S60 or V60 diesel is worth £3,000-£12,000 depending on mileage and condition. For a sub-£4,000 example, EGR or DPF replacement costs may represent 10-20% of vehicle value - a repair is usually justified. For cars with multiple simultaneous failures, evaluate whether replacement makes more sense.
problems.recommendation: EGR and DPF issues are the most common problems facing S60 and V60 diesel owners. Regular motorway driving helps keep the DPF clear. If you're experiencing power loss or warning lights, have the EGR valve inspected first - a simple clean may resolve the issue. If the EGR valve has failed completely, replacement with a genuine Volvo part is recommended (specialist cost £450-£700).
problems.cta: -> Compare Volvo S60 / V60 diesel EGR and DPF repair costs

problems.h4: Injector Failure - Volvo S60 / V60 D5 Diesel
problems.rootCause: Unreliable fuel injectors are one of the biggest problems for D5 owners. Injector failure leads to rough running, smoky exhaust, poor cold starting and increased fuel consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: If injector failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 2010-2013 S60 or V60 D5 worth £3,000-£7,000, a £1,000-£1,800 full injector set is a significant but justifiable repair. If the engine has suffered consequential damage from injector failure, a rebuilt engine with warranty becomes the better option.
problems.recommendation: Injector failure on the D5 is a well-known issue. If you're experiencing rough running or poor cold starting, have the injectors tested. Replacing all five injectors (specialist cost £1,000-£1,800) is recommended for high-mileage units - doing one at a time often costs more in the long run. If the engine has been damaged by injector failure, a rebuilt unit with warranty is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare Volvo S60 / V60 D5 injector replacement costs

problems.h4: Timing Belt Failure - Volvo S60 / V60 All Diesel Variants
problems.affectedModels: Volvo S60 and V60 (all D3, D4 and D5 diesel variants)
problems.rootCause: The D3, D4 and D5 diesel engines use a timing belt rather than a chain. If the auxiliary belt or pulley fails, it can take the timing belt with it and wreck the engine. Tensioners are prone to failure and may not last the scheduled interval.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New belt, tensioner, pulleys, water pump
If belt has snapped causing valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For any S60 or V60 diesel, a £450-£800 timing belt replacement is excellent value compared to a £3,500-£6,500 engine replacement. This is one of the most important preventative maintenance items.
problems.recommendation: Timing belt failure is catastrophic and entirely preventable. Volvo recommends replacement every 140,000 km (approx 87,000 miles) or 10 years, but many specialists recommend 60,000-80,000 miles or 8 years. If you have no record of the timing belt being changed, assume it hasn't been and budget for replacement immediately. This is the single most important investment you can make in your S60 or V60 diesel.
problems.cta: -> Compare Volvo S60 / V60 diesel timing belt replacement costs

problems.h4: Oil Consumption - Volvo S60 / V60 2.0-litre Drive-E Diesel (D4204T9, D4204T14, D4204T11)
problems.affectedModels: Volvo S60 and V60 D3 and D4 (D4204T9, D4204T14), D5 (D4204T11) - pre-2016 units
problems.rootCause: Pre-2016 VEA (Drive-E) diesel engines can be prone to developing high oil consumption. The most probable reason is pre-2016 piston oil rings. Piston rings were modified in mid-2016. Volvo considered 0.5 litres per 1,000 km oil consumption as "normal".

repairOptions.longevity: If consumption is within Volvo's "normal" range

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full strip-down, new pistons and rings
Supply & fit rebuilt unit with upgraded rings
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term value if keeping car

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 2014-2016 S60 or V60 D4 worth £4,000-£10,000, a £2,000-£3,500 piston ring replacement is significant. If the car is worth under £5,000, evaluate whether replacement is justified versus a used engine or scrapping.
problems.recommendation: Oil consumption on pre-2016 VEA diesels is a known issue. If your car is consuming more than 1 litre per 1,000 miles and you plan to keep the car, a rebuilt engine with upgraded piston rings is the definitive fix. For lower-value examples, consider a quality used engine or evaluate whether the repair is justified.
